dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I heard that the maple leaves back home have already turned red. I want to go back and take a look, but it's a long journey. I can't return for now...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I was wandering the market the other day and saw these well-preserved maple leaves, so I bought some.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Although I can't confirm whether they're from my hometown, they still help blunt my homesickness.

choices.text: You're very fond of maple leaves, then?

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: In the past, I collected maple leaves upon the autumnal winds and carried them on my person.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: When I was on the boat, I scattered them across the surface of the ocean and watched them float to distant shores.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Perhaps another homesick soul will have picked up one of those leaves...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I also want to see your hometown.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: I should have taken the initiative to invite you... But I was absorbed by my own homesickness.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Then take this maple leaf as a keepsake. Our promise is thus made.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: When the maple leaves next bloom red, we shall go to my hometown together.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Indeed... From a purely visual perspective, red maple leaves have a unique beauty to them.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Every year in my hometown, people enjoy the scene of falling red leaves.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: The maple leaves are a crimson sunset and fall like scarlet rain.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: A thick layer of fallen leaves on the ground, the chirping of autumn insects, and the wandering birds...
